paragraphs: Unless otherwise indicated or unless the context requires otherwise, references to "we," "our," "us" and "our company" refer to American Assets Trust, Inc., a Maryland corporation, together with our consolidated subsidiaries, including American Assets Trust, L.P., a Maryland limited partnership, of which we are the sole general partner and which we refer to in this report as our Operating Partnership. In statements regarding qualification as a REIT, such terms refer solely to American Assets Trust, Inc.

We are a full service, vertically integrated and self-administered real estate investment trust, or REIT, that owns, operates, acquires and develops high quality office, retail, multifamily and mixed-use properties in attractive, high-barrier-to-entry markets in Southern California, Northern California, Washington, Oregon, Texas and Hawaii. As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio is comprised of twelve office properties; eleven retail shopping centers; a mixed-use property consisting of a 369-room all-suite hotel and a retail shopping center; and seven multifamily properties. Additionally, as of December 31, 2025, we owned land at two of our properties that we classified as held for development and construction in progress. Our core markets include San Diego, California; the San Francisco Bay Area, California; Bellevue, Washington; Portland, Oregon and Oahu, Hawaii.

American Assets Trust, Inc. is a Maryland corporation that was formed on July 16, 2010 to acquire the entities owning various controlling and noncontrolling interests in real estate assets owned and/or managed by Ernest S. Rady or his affiliates, including the Ernest Rady Trust U/D/T March 13, 1983, or the Rady Trust, and did not have any operating activity until the consummation of our initial public offering and the related acquisition of such interest on January 19, 2011. After the completion of our initial public offering and the related acquisitions, our operations have been carried on through our Operating Partnership. American Assets Trust, Inc., as the sole general partner of our Operating Partnership, has control of our Operating Partnership and owned 78.95% of our Operating Partnership as of December 31, 2025. Accordingly, we consolidate the assets, liabilities and results of operations of our Operating Partnership.

We believe the following competitive strengths distinguish us from other owners and operators of commercial real estate and will enable us to take advantage of new acquisition and development opportunities, as well as growth opportunities within our portfolio:

•Irreplaceable Portfolio of High Quality Office, Retail and Multifamily Properties. We have acquired and developed a high quality portfolio of office, retail and multifamily properties located in affluent neighborhoods and sought-after business centers in San Diego, California, the San Francisco Bay Area, California, Bellevue, Washington; Portland, Oregon; San Antonio, Texas and Oahu, Hawaii. Many of our properties are located in in-fill locations where developable land is scarce or where we believe current zoning, environmental and entitlement regulations significantly restrict new development. We believe that the location of many of our properties will provide us an advantage in terms of generating higher internal revenue growth on a relative basis.
•Experienced and Committed Senior Management Team with Strong Sponsorship. The members of our senior management team have significant experience in all aspects of the commercial real estate industry.

•Properties Located in High-Barrier-to-Entry Markets with Strong Real Estate Fundamentals. Our core markets currently include Southern California, Northern California, Washington, Oregon and Hawaii, which we believe have attractive long-term real estate fundamentals driven by favorable supply and demand characteristics.

•Extensive Market Knowledge and Long-Standing Relationships Facilitate Access to a Pipeline of Acquisition and Leasing Opportunities. We believe that our in-depth market knowledge and extensive network of long-standing relationships in the real estate industry provide us access to an ongoing pipeline of attractive acquisition and investment opportunities in and near our core markets, while also facilitating our leasing efforts and providing us with opportunities to increase occupancy rates at our properties.

•Internal Growth Prospects through Development, Redevelopment and Repositioning. The development and redevelopment potential at several of our properties presents compelling growth prospects and our expertise enhances our ability to capitalize on these opportunities.

•Broad Real Estate Expertise with Office, Retail and Multifamily Focus. Our senior management team has strong experience and capabilities across the real estate sector with significant expertise in the office, retail and multifamily asset classes, which provides for flexibility in pursuing attractive acquisition, development and repositioning opportunities. Ernest Rady, our Executive Chairman, Adam Wyll, our President and Chief Executive Officer, and Robert Barton, our Chief Financial Officer, and the other members of senior management, each have over 25 years of commercial real estate experience.

Our primary business objectives are to increase operating cash flows, generate long-term growth and maximize stockholder value. Specifically, we pursue the following strategies to achieve these objectives:

•Capitalizing on Acquisition Opportunities in High-Barrier-to-Entry Markets. We intend to pursue growth through the strategic acquisition of attractively priced, high quality properties that are well located in their submarkets, focusing on markets that generally are characterized by strong supply and demand characteristics, including high barriers to entry and diverse industry bases, that appeal to institutional investors.

•Repositioning/Redevelopment and Development of Office, Retail and Multifamily Properties. Our strategy is to selectively reposition and redevelop several of our existing or newly-acquired properties, and we will also selectively pursue ground-up development of undeveloped land where we believe we can generate attractive risk-adjusted returns.

•Disciplined Capital Recycling Strategy. Our strategy is to pursue an efficient asset allocation strategy that maximizes the value of our investments by selectively disposing of properties whose returns appear to have been maximized and redeploying capital into acquisition, repositioning, redevelopment and development opportunities with higher return prospects, in each case in a manner that is consistent with our qualification as a REIT.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
We may be adversely affected by trends in office real estate.
We have a substantial amount of indebtedness, which may expose us to the risk of default under our debt obligations.
Our retail shopping center properties depend on anchor stores or major tenants to attract shoppers and could be adversely affected by the loss of, or a store closure by, one or more of these tenants.
We may be unable to identify and complete acquisitions of properties that meet our criteria, which may impede our growth.
We face significant competition for acquisitions of real properties, which may reduce the number of acquisition opportunities available to us and increase the costs of these acquisitions.
Our ability to grow will be limited if we cannot obtain additional capital.
Mortgage debt obligations expose us to the possibility of foreclosure, which could result in the loss of our investment in a property or group of properties subject to mortgage debt.
We may not be able to control our operating costs or our expenses may remain constant or increase, even if our revenues do not increase, causing our results of operations to be adversely affected.
Some of our financing arrangements involve balloon payment obligations, which may adversely affect our ability to make distributions.
Failure to hedge effectively against interest rate changes may adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations, cash flow and per share trading price of our common stock.
The effective subordination of our unsecured indebtedness may reduce amounts available for payment on our unsecured indebtedness.

If we invest in mortgage receivables, including originating mortgages, such investment would be subject to several risks, any of which could decrease the value of such investments and result in a significant loss to us.
Changes in Trade Policies, Including the Imposition of Tariffs, Could Adversely Affect Our Tenants, Ability to Lease Space, Development Activities, and Operating Costs
A Prolonged Federal Government Shutdown Could Adversely Affect Some of Our Tenants
We face significant competition in the leasing market, which may decrease or prevent increases of the occupancy and rental rates of our properties.

We may acquire properties or portfolios of properties through tax deferred contribution transactions, which could result in stockholder dilution and limit our ability to sell or refinance such assets.
Embassy Suites™, our franchisor, has a right of first offer with respect to the Waikiki Beach Walk-Embassy Suites™, which may limit our ability to obtain the highest price possible for the hotel.
Potential losses from earthquakes, fires, floods or other natural disasters may not be fully covered by insurance.
We may be adversely affected by laws, regulations or other issues related to climate change.
Climate change may adversely impact our properties directly, and may lead to additional compliance obligations and costs as well as additional taxes and fees.
paragraphs: The following section includes the most significant factors that may adversely affect our business and operations. The risk factors describe risks that may affect these statements but are not all-inclusive, particularly with respect to possible future events. Moreover, we operate in a very competitive and rapidly changing environment. New risk factors emerge from time to time and it is not possible for us to predict all such risk factors, nor can we assess the impact of all such risk factors on our business or the extent to which any factor, or combination of factors, may cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in any forward-looking statements. This discussion of risk factors includes many forward-looking statements. For cautions about relying on forward-looking statements, please refer to the section entitled "Forward Looking Statements" at the beginning of this Report immediately prior to Item 1.

Our portfolio of properties is dependent upon regional and local economic conditions and is geographically concentrated in California, Washington, Oregon, Texas and Hawaii, which may cause us to be more susceptible to adverse developments in those markets than if we owned a more geographically diverse portfolio.

Our properties are located in California, Washington, Oregon, Texas and Hawaii, and substantially all of our properties are concentrated in California, Washington, Oregon and Hawaii, which exposes us to greater economic risks than if we owned a more geographically diverse portfolio. As a result, we are particularly susceptible to adverse economic or other conditions in these markets (such as periods of economic slowdown or recession, business layoffs or downsizing, industry slowdowns, changes in the local or global tourism industry, relocations of businesses, increases in real estate and other taxes and the cost of complying with governmental regulations or increased regulation), as well as to natural disasters that occur in these markets (such as earthquakes, wildfires, tropical storms, hurricanes, tornadoes and other events). If there is a downturn in the economy in these markets, our operations and our revenue and cash available for distribution, including cash available to pay distributions to American Assets Trust, Inc.'s stockholders or American Assets Trust, L.P.'s unitholders, could be materially adversely affected. We cannot assure you that these markets will grow or that underlying real estate fundamentals will be favorable to owners and operators of office, retail, mixed-use or multifamily properties. Our operations may also be affected if competing properties are built in any of these markets. Moreover, submarkets within any of our core markets may be dependent upon a limited number of industries. In addition, the State of California is regarded as more litigious, highly regulated and taxed than many other states, all of which may reduce demand for office, retail, mixed-use or multifamily space in California. Any adverse economic or real estate developments in the California, Washington, Oregon, Texas or Hawaii markets, or any decrease in demand for office, retail, multifamily or mixed-use space resulting from the regulatory environment, business climate or energy or fiscal problems, could adversely impact our financial condition, results of operations, cash flow, our ability to satisfy our debt service obligations and our ability to pay distributions to American Assets Trust, Inc.'s stockholders or American Assets Trust, L.P.'s unitholders.

In 2025, approximately 52% of our net operating income was from our office properties. Work from home, flexible work schedules, open workplaces, videoconferencing, and teleconferencing have become common, particularly as a result of the pandemic. These practices may enable businesses to reduce their office space requirements. There is also an increasing trend among some businesses to utilize shared office spaces and co-working spaces. A continuation of the movement towards these practices could, over time, erode the overall demand for office space and, in turn, place downward pressure on occupancy, rental rates and property valuations, which may adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and cash flow.

At February 6, 2026, we had total debt outstanding of $1.70 billion, excluding debt issuance costs, a portion of which contains non-recourse carve-out guarantees and environmental indemnities from us and our Operating Partnership, and we may incur significant additional debt to finance future acquisition and development activities. At December 31, 2025, we also had a third amended and restated credit facility with a capacity of $500 million, consisting of a revolving line of credit of $400 million and an unsecured term loan of $100 million (Term Loan A). Payments of principal and interest on borrowings may leave us with insufficient cash resources to operate our properties or to pay the dividends currently contemplated or necessary to maintain our REIT qualification. We are a full service, vertically integrated and self-administered REIT that owns, operates, acquires and develops high quality office, retail, multifamily and mixed-use properties in attractive, high-barrier-to-entry markets in Southern California, Northern California, Washington, Oregon, Texas, and Hawaii. As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio was comprised of twelve office properties; eleven retail shopping centers; a mixed-use property consisting of a 369-room all-suite hotel and a retail shopping center; and seven multifamily properties. Additionally, as of December 31, 2025, we owned land at two of our properties that we classified as held for development or construction in progress. La Jolla Commons - Land, related to the development of La Jolla Commons III, was previously classified as held for development. The development of La Jolla Commons III is now complete and the building, inclusive of the land, was placed in operations as of April 1, 2025. Our core markets include San Diego, California; the San Francisco Bay Area, California; Bellevue, Washington; Portland, Oregon, and Oahu, Hawaii. American Assets Trust, Inc., as the sole general partner of our Operating Partnership, has control of our Operating Partnership and owned 78.95% of our Operating Partnership as of December 31, 2025. Accordingly, we consolidate the assets, liabilities and results of operations of our Operating Partnership.

On November 5, 2010, we formed American Assets Services, Inc., a Delaware corporation that is wholly owned by our Operating Partnership and which we refer to as our services company. We have elected, together with our services company, to treat our services company as a taxable REIT subsidiary for federal income tax purposes. A taxable REIT subsidiary generally may provide non-customary and other services to our tenants and engage in activities that we may not engage in directly without adversely affecting our qualification as a REIT, provided a taxable REIT subsidiary may not operate or manage a lodging facility or provide rights to any brand name under which any lodging facility is operated. We may form additional taxable REIT subsidiaries in the future, and our Operating Partnership may contribute some or all of its interests in certain wholly owned subsidiaries or their assets to our services company. Any income earned by our taxable REIT subsidiaries will not be included in our taxable income for purposes of the 75% or 95% gross income tests, except to the extent such income is distributed to us as a dividend, in which case such dividend income will qualify under the 95%, but not the 75%, gross income test. Because a taxable REIT subsidiary is subject to federal income tax and state and local income tax (where applicable) as a regular corporation, the income earned by our taxable REIT subsidiaries generally will be subject to an additional level of tax as compared to the income earned by our other subsidiaries.

We seek growth in earnings, funds from operations, and cash flows primarily through a combination of the following: growth in our same-store portfolio, growth in our portfolio from property development and redevelopments and expansion of our portfolio through property acquisitions. Our properties are located in some of the nation's most dynamic, high-barrier-to-entry markets primarily in Southern California, Northern California, Washington, Oregon and Hawaii, which we believe allow us to take advantage of redevelopment opportunities that enhance our operating performance through renovation, expansion, reconfiguration, and/or retenanting. We evaluate our properties on an ongoing basis to identify these types of opportunities.

We intend to opportunistically pursue projects in our development pipeline, including future phases of Lloyd Portfolio, other redevelopments at Waikele Center, as well as multifamily development opportunities within our existing portfolio, namely at Lomas Santa Fe Plaza, Solana Beach Towne Centre, Carmel Mountain Plaza, and Genesee Park. The commencement of these developments is based on, among other things, market conditions and our evaluation of whether such opportunities would generate appropriate risk-adjusted financial returns. Our redevelopment and development opportunities are subject to various factors, including market conditions and may not ultimately come to fruition. We continue to review acquisition opportunities in our primary markets that would complement our portfolio and provide long-term growth opportunities. Some of our acquisitions do not initially contribute significantly to earnings growth; however, we believe they provide long-term re-leasing growth, redevelopment opportunities and other strategic opportunities. Any growth from acquisitions is contingent on our ability to find properties that meet our qualitative standards at prices that meet our financial hurdles. Changes in interest rates may affect our success in achieving earnings growth through acquisitions by affecting both the price that must be paid to acquire a property, as well as our ability to economically finance a property acquisition. Generally, our acquisitions are initially financed by available cash, mortgage loans and/or borrowings under our credit facility, which may be repaid later with funds raised through the issuance of new equity or new long-term debt.

We have provided certain information on a total portfolio, same-store and redevelopment same-store basis. Information provided on a same-store basis includes the results of properties that we owned and operated for the entirety of both periods being compared except for properties for which significant redevelopment or expansion occurred during either of the periods being compared, properties under development, properties classified as held for development and properties classified as discontinued operations. Information provided on a redevelopment same-store basis includes the results of properties undergoing significant redevelopment for the entirety or portion of both periods being compared. Same-store and redevelopment same-store are considered by management to be important measures because they assist in eliminating disparities due to the development, acquisition or disposition of properties during the particular period presented, and thus provide a more consistent performance measure for the comparison of the company's stabilized and redevelopment properties, as applicable. Additionally, redevelopment same-store is considered by management to be an important measure because it assists in evaluating the timing of the start and stabilization of our redevelopment opportunities and the impact that these redevelopments have in enhancing our operating performance.

While there is judgment surrounding changes in designations, we typically reclassify significant development, redevelopment or expansion properties into same-store properties once they are stabilized. Properties are deemed stabilized typically at the earlier of (1) reaching 90% occupancy or (2) four quarters following a property's inclusion in operating real estate. We typically remove properties from same-store properties when the development, redevelopment or expansion has or is expected to have a significant impact on the property's annualized base rent, occupancy and operating income within the calendar year. Our evaluation of significant impact related to development, redevelopment or expansion activity is based on quantitative and qualitative measures including, but not limited to, the following: the total budgeted cost of planned construction activity compared to the property's annualized base rent, occupancy and operating income within the calendar year; percentage of development, redevelopment or expansion square footage to total property square footage; and the ability to maintain historic occupancy and rental rates. In consideration of these measures, we generally remove properties from same-store properties when we see a decline in a property's annualized base rent, occupancy and operating income within the calendar year as a direct result of ongoing redevelopment, development or expansion activity. Acquired properties are classified into same-store properties once we have owned such properties for the entirety of comparable period(s) and the properties are not under significant development or expansion.

Below is a summary of our same-store composition for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023. One Beach Street is identified as a non-same-store property for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, due to significant redevelopment activity. Additionally, this property was placed into operations on August 1, 2024, approximately one year after completing renovations. Del Monte Center was removed as a same-store property when compared to the designations for the year ended December 31, 2024, as it was sold on February 25, 2025. Genesee Park is classified as a non-same-store property because it was acquired on February 28, 2025, and thus has not been owned for the comparable period. La Jolla Commons III is classified as a non-same store property when compared to the designations for the year ended December 31, 2024, as it was placed in operations on April 1, 2025. La Jolla Commons III is a part of the La Jolla Commons office project, and not a stand-alone property.

For the year ended December 31, 2024, when compared to the designations for the year ended December 31, 2023, Timber Springs was classified as a same-store property for the year ended December 31, 2024, because the property was acquired on March 8, 2022. The 710 building within the Lloyd Portfolio was classified as a same-store property when compared to the designation for the year ended December 31, 2023, because the property had been in operation for a full year since it was placed in service in November 2022. One Beach Street is identified as a non-same-store property for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, due to significant redevelopment activity. Additionally, this property was placed into operations on August 1, 2024, approximately one year after completing renovations.

Rental income consists of scheduled rent charges, straight-line rent adjustments and the amortization of above market and below market rents acquired. We also derive revenue from tenant recoveries and other property revenues, including parking income, lease termination fees, late fees, storage rents and other miscellaneous property revenues.

Office Leases. Our office portfolio included twelve properties with a total of approximately 4.3 million rentable square feet available for lease as of December 31, 2025. As of December 31, 2025, these properties were 83.1% leased. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the office segment contributed 47.2% of our total revenue. Historically, we have leased office properties to tenants primarily on a full service gross or a modified gross basis and to a limited extent on a triple-net lease basis. We expect to continue to do so in the future. A full-service gross or modified gross lease has a base year expense stop, whereby the tenant pays a stated amount of certain expenses as part of the rent payment, while future increases in property operating expenses (above the base year stop) are billed to the tenant based on such tenant's proportionate square footage of the property. The increased property operating expenses billed are reflected as operating expenses and amounts recovered from tenants are reflected as rental income in the statements of operations.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, we signed 82 office leases for 616,680 square feet with an average rent of $55.50 per square foot during the initial year of the lease term. Of the leases, 46 represent comparable leases where there was a prior tenant, with an increase of 6.4% in cash basis rent and an increase of 13.8% in straight-line rent compared to the prior leases.

Retail Leases. Our retail portfolio included eleven properties with a total of approximately 2.4 million rentable square feet available for lease as of December 31, 2025. As of December 31, 2025, these properties were 97.7% leased. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the retail segment contributed 21.8%, of our total revenue. Historically, we have leased retail properties to tenants primarily on a triple-net lease basis, and we expect to continue to do so in the future. In a triple-net lease, the tenant is responsible for all property taxes and operating expenses. As such, the base rent payment does not include any operating expense, but rather all such expenses, to the extent they are paid by the landlord, are billed to the tenant. The full amount of the expenses for this lease type, to the extent they are paid by the landlord, is reflected in operating expenses, and the reimbursement is reflected as rental income in the statements of operations.

paragraphs: 除非另有說明或上下文另有要求，文中所稱「我們」、「我們的」、「我們」及「本公司」均指美國資產信託股份有限公司，為馬裏蘭州公司，與我們合併的子公司，包括美國資產信託有限合夥企業，為馬裏蘭州有限合夥企業，我們為其唯一的一般合夥人，並在本報告中稱為我們的營運合夥企業。在有關符合REIT資格的陳述中，這些詞彙僅指美國資產信託股份有限公司。

我們是一家全服務、垂直整合且自營的商業不動產投資信託，或稱REIT，擁有、經營、取得及開發位於美國南加州、北加州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、德克薩斯州及夏威夷州等具吸引力且高門檻市場的高品質辦公室、零售、多戶住宅及混合用途不動產。截至2025年12月31日，我們的資產組合包含十二處辦公室不動產；十一處零售購物中心；一處混合用途不動產，包含369間全套房酒店及零售購物中心；以及七處多戶住宅不動產。此外，截至2025年12月31日，我們在兩處不動產中擁有土地，並歸類為持有以開發及建設進行中。我們的核心市場包括加州聖地牙哥；加州舊金山灣區；華盛頓州貝爾維尤；俄勒岡州波特蘭及夏威夷州歐胡島。

美國資產信託股份有限公司為馬裏蘭州公司，於2010年7月16日成立，以取得擁有Ernest S. Rady或其關係企業所擁有及/或管理的各項控制及非控制權益的實體，包括Ernest Rady信託，於1983年3月13日設立，或稱Rady信託，並在2011年1月19日完成首次公開發行及相關取得這些權益之前，沒有任何營運活動。完成首次公開發行及相關取得後，我們的營運均透過營運合夥企業進行。美國資產信託股份有限公司作為營運合夥企業的唯一一般合夥人，控制營運合夥企業，並於2025年12月31日持有營運合夥企業78.95%的權益。因此，我們將營運合夥企業的資產、負債及營運結果納入合併財務報表。
我們認為以下競爭優勢使我們與其他商業不動產所有者及經營者有所區別，並能讓我們把握新的取得及開發機會，以及在資產組合內的成長機會：

•不可取代的高品質辦公室、零售及多戶住宅不動產組合。我們已取得並開發位於加州聖地牙哥、加州舊金山灣區、華盛頓州貝爾維尤；俄勒岡州波特蘭；德克薩斯州聖安東尼奧及夏威夷州歐胡島等富裕社區及受歡迎的商業中心的高品質辦公室、零售及多戶住宅不動產。我們許多不動產位於填海地段，開發用地稀少，或我們認為現行 zoning、環境及許可規範顯著限制新開發。我們相信，許多不動產的地理位置將使我們在相對基礎上產生更高的內部營收成長。
•經驗豐富且投入的高階管理團隊與強大後盾。我們高階管理團隊的成員在商業不動產產業的各個方面均有豐富經驗。
•位於高門檻市場的不動產，具備強勁的不動產基本面。我們的核心市場目前包括南加州、北加州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州及夏威夷州，我們認為這些市場具有吸引人的長期不動產基本面，由有利的供需特徵所驅動。
•廣泛的市場知識與長期關係有助於取得取得及租賃機會的管道。我們相信，我們深入的市場知識及在不動產產業中廣泛的長期關係網路，使我們能取得持續的取得及投資機會，位於或接近我們的核心市場，同時也促進我們的租賃努力，並提供我們提高不動產佔用率的機會。
•透過開發、再開發與重新定位來實現內在成長潛力。我們在數個不動產的開發與再開發潛力，呈現出強勁的成長前景，而我們的專業知識增強了我們把握這些機會的能力。

•具備廣泛不動產專業知識，專注於辦公室、零售與多家庭住宅。我們的高階管理團隊在不動產領域擁有強大的經驗與能力，尤其在辦公室、零售與多家庭住宅資產類別方面有顯著的專業知識，這使我們在追求具吸引力的收購、開發與重新定位機會時更具靈活性。Ernest Rady，我們的執行 chairman，Adam Wyll，我們的董事長兼首席執行官，以及 Robert Barton，我們的首席財務官，以及其他高階管理團隊成員，每人皆擁有超過 25 年的商業不動產經驗。
我們的主要業務目標為增加營運現金流、產生長期成長並最大化股東價值。具體而言，我們透過以下策略來達成這些目標：
•把握高門檻市場的收購機會。我們意圖透過戰略性收購具吸引力價格、高品質且位於其次市場優良地段的不動產來實現成長，專注於一般具強勁供需特質、包括高門檻與多元產業基礎的市場，這些市場對機構投資者具有吸引力。
•辦公室、零售與多家庭住宅不動產的重新定位/再開發與開發。我們的策略為選擇性地重新定位與再開發我們現有或新近收購的不動產，同時也會選擇性地進行未開發土地的從零開始開發，我們相信這能產生具吸引力的風險調整後回報。
•嚴謹的資本循環策略。我們的策略為追求一個高效的資產配置策略，透過選擇性地處置回報似乎已達極致的不動產，並將資金重新配置至具更高回報潛力的收購、重新定位、再開發與開發機會，以符合我們作為 REIT 的資格。

paragraphs: 下列討論應與本報告「第 8 項 財務報表及補充資料」中出現的審計歷史合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。在本節中，除非文意另有要求，否則「我們」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們公司」均指美國資產信託股份有限公司，為馬裏蘭州公司及其合併子公司，包括美國資產信託有限公司。在有關符合 REIT 資格的陳述中，這些詞彙僅指美國資產信託股份有限公司。本討論可能包含基於當前預期的展望性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。我們的實際結果可能與這些展望性陳述中預期的有重大差異，這是因為各種因素，包括在「第 1A 項 風險因素」或本文件其他地方所列舉的因素。請參閱「第 1A 項 風險因素」及「展望性陳述」。

我們是一家全功能、垂直整合且自營的 REIT，擁有、營運、取得並開發位於美國南加州、北加州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、德州及夏威夷州等具吸引力且高門檻市場的高品質辦公室、零售、多戶住宅及混合用途不動產。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的投資組合包含十二處辦公室不動產；十一處零售購物中心；一處混合用途不動產，包含 369 房間的全套房酒店及零售購物中心；以及七處多戶住宅不動產。此外，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在兩處不動產中擁有土地，並歸類為持有待開發或建設進行中。La Jolla Commons - Land，與 La Jolla Commons III 的開發有關，先前歸類為持有待開發。La Jolla Commons III 的開發現已完工，包含土地的建築物於 2025 年 4 月 1 日投入運作。我們的核心市場包括加州聖地牙哥；加州舊金山灣區；華盛頓州 Bellevue；俄勒岡州波特蘭，以及夏威夷州 Oahu。美國資產信託股份有限公司作為我們營運合夥企業的唯一普通合夥人，控制我們的營運合夥企業，並於 2025 年 12 月 31 日擁有其 78.95% 的權益。因此，我們合併我們營運合夥企業的資產、負債及營運結果。

2010 年 11 月 5 日，我們成立了美國資產服務股份有限公司，為德拉瓦州公司，為我們營運合夥企業的 wholly owned 並稱為我們的服務公司。我們已選擇，與我們的服務公司共同，將我們的服務公司視為美國聯邦所得稅目的的可課稅 REIT 子公司。可課稅 REIT 子公司通常可為我們的租戶提供非慣例及其他服務，並進行我們可能無法直接進行的活動，而不會影響我們作為 REIT 的資格，前提是可課稅 REIT 子公司不得經營或管理旅館設施，或提供任何旅館設施運營的品牌名稱。我們可能在未來成立更多的可課稅 REIT 子公司，並且我們的營運合夥企業可能將其在某些 wholly owned 子公司的權益或其資產貢獻給我們的服務公司。我們可課稅 REIT 子公司所賺取的收入，不計入我們的應稅收入，以符合 75% 或 95% 的毛收入測試，除非這些收入以股息形式分發給我們，此時這些股息收入符合 95% 的測試，但不包括 75% 的測試。因為可課稅 REIT 子公司作為普通公司需納美國聯邦所得稅及州及地方所得稅（如適用），因此我們可課稅 REIT 子公司所賺取的收入通常會比我們其他子公司所賺取的收入多一層稅務負擔。

我們主要透過以下方式追求 earnings、 funds from operations 及 cash flows 的成長：(1) 我們同店投資組合的成長；(2) 我們投資組合因不動產開發及重新開發而成長；(3) 透過不動產取得擴充我們的投資組合。我們的不動產位於美國一些最動態、高門檻市場，主要在南加州、北加州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州及夏威夷州，我們認為這些市場使我們能利用重新開發機會，透過翻修、擴建、重新配置及/或重新出租來提升我們的營運表現。我們持續評估我們的不動產，以識別這些類型的機會。

我們有意在開發管道中機會性地追求項目，包括 Lloyd Portfolio 的未來階段、Waikele Center 的其他重新開發，以及我們現有投資組合內的多戶住宅開發機會，即 Lomas Santa Fe Plaza、Solana Beach Towne Centre、Carmel Mountain Plaza 及 Genesee Park。這些開發的啟動取決於市場條件及我們評估這些機會是否能產生適當的風險調整後財務回報。我們的重新開發及開發機會受到多種因素影響，包括市場條件，且可能最終無法實現。我們持續評估我們主要市場中的收購機會，這些機會能補強我們的投資組合並提供長期成長機會。我們的一些收購初期對 earnings 成長的貢獻不大；然而，我們認為這些收購提供了長期重新出租成長、重新開發機會及其他戰略機會。任何來自收購的成長取決於我們能否找到符合我們品質標準且價格符合我們財務門檻的不動產。利率的變化可能影響我們透過收購實現 earnings 成長的成功，因為這會影響我們必須支付的收購價格，以及我們經濟性融資收購不動產的能力。通常，我們的收購最初由現金、抵押貸款及/或信用融資的貸款資金進行，這些資金可能在後續透過發行新股或新長期債務來償還。

我們已提供某些資訊，以總體投資組合、同店及重新開發同店為基礎。以同店為基礎提供的資訊包括我們擁有並營運的不動產結果，這些不動產在比較期間的整個期間內擁有並營運，除非有重大重新開發或擴建發生在比較期間的任何期間，或在開發中的不動產、歸類為持有待開發及歸類為已終止營運的不動產。以重新開發同店為基礎提供的資訊包括在比較期間的整個期間或部分期間內進行重大重新開發的不動產結果。同店及重新開發同店被管理層視為重要的衡量指標，因為它們有助於消除因特定期間內不動產的開發、取得或處分而產生的差異，並提供更一致的表現衡量指標，用以比較公司的穩定不動產及重新開發不動產，如適用。此外，重新開發同店被管理層視為重要的衡量指標，因為它有助於評估我們重新開發機會的持續進行，以及我們的年度毛租金、佔用率及營運收入的下降。

以下是我們同店組成的總結，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日。One Beach Street 被識別為非同店不動產，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日，因有重大重新開發活動。此外，該不動產於 2024 年 8 月 1 日投入運作，距離完成翻修約一年。Del Monte Center 在與 2024 年 12 月 31 日的歸類比較時被移除為同店不動產，因其於 2025 年 2 月 25 日出售。Genesee Park 被歸類為非同店不動產，因其於 2025 年 2 月 28 日取得，因此尚未擁有可比期間。La Jolla Commons III 在與 2024 年 12 月 31 日的歸類比較時被歸類為非同店不動產，因其於 2025 年 4 月 1 日投入運作。La Jolla Commons III 是 La Jolla Commons 辦公室專案的一部分，而非獨立不動產。

以下是我們同店組成的總結，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日。One Beach Street 被識別為非同店不動產，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日，因有重大重新開發活動。此外，該不動產於 2024 年 8 月 1 日投入運作，距離完成翻修約一年。Del Monte Center 在與 2024 年 12 月 31 日的歸類比較時被移除為同店不動產，因其於 2025 年 2 月 25 日出售。Genesee Park 被歸類為非同店不動產，因其於 2025 年 2 月 28 日取得，因此尚未擁有可比期間。La Jolla Commons III 在與 2024 年 12 月 31 日的歸類比較時被歸類為非同店不動產，因其於 2025 年 4 月 1 日投入運作。La Jolla Commons III 是 La Jolla Commons 辦公室專案的一部分，而非獨立不動產。

會計年度終了日為2024年12月31日，與2023年12月31日的分類相比，Timber Springs 被歸類為同店舖財產，因為該財產於2022年3月8日取得。Lloyd Portfolio 內的710大樓與2023年12月31日的分類相比，被歸類為同店舖財產，因為該財產自2022年11月投入營運後已運作滿一年。One Beach Street 被歸類為非同店舖財產，於2024年及2023年會計年度終了日為12月31日，因其進行了重大重建活動。此外，該財產於2024年8月1日投入營運，距離完成裝修約一年時間。
租金收入包含預定租金、直線租金調整及市場租金以上市場租金與以下市場租金的攤銷。我們亦從租戶補償及其他財產收入中獲取收入，包括停車收入、租約終止費用、遲交費用、儲存租金及其他雜項財產收入。

辦公室租賃。我們的辦公室資產組合包含十二處財產，於2025年12月31日時，總計約有4.3百萬平方英呎的可出租面積。於2025年12月31日時，這些財產的出租率為83.1%。於2025年12月31日會計年度終了時，辦公室部門貢獻了我們總營收的47.2%。歷來，我們主要以全服務毛租或改良毛租方式出租辦公室財產，並有限度以三重淨租方式出租。我們預期未來也會持續如此。全服務毛租或改良毛租有基準年費用停止點，租戶需支付特定費用的固定金額作為租金的一部分，而未來財產營運費用的增加（超過基準年停止點）則根據租戶所佔的財產平方英呎比例向租戶收取。增加的財產營運費用會反映在營運費用中，而從租戶收取的金額則會反映在營運損益表的租金收入中。
於2025年12月31日會計年度終了時，我們簽訂了82份辦公室租賃合約，總計約616,680平方英呎，於租賃合約初始年份的平均租金為每平方英呎55.50美元。其中46份為可比租賃合約，有先前租戶，與先前租賃合約相比，現金基礎租金增加了6.4%，直線租金增加了13.8%。

零售租賃。我們的零售資產組合包含十一處財產，於2025年12月31日時，總計約有2.4百萬平方英呎的可出租面積。於2025年12月31日時，這些財產的出租率為97.7%。於2025年12月31日會計年度終了時，零售部門貢獻了我們總營收的21.8%。歷來，我們主要以三重淨租方式出租零售財產，並預期未來也會持續如此。在三重淨租中，租戶需承擔所有財產稅及營運費用。因此，基本租金支付不包含任何營運費用，而所有營運費用（如由地主支付）則會向租戶收取。此種租賃類型的全部費用（如由地主支付），會反映在營運費用中，而補償金額則會反映在營運損益表的租金收入中。

headings: 與本公司業務及營運相關之風險
我們可能因辦公室實體地產趨勢而受到負面影響。
本公司負擔相當程度之債務，這可能使我們面臨違約我們債務義務之風險。
我們之零售購物中心不動產依賴主要租戶或大型租客吸引消費者，若這些租戶之一或數個離場或關閉營業，可能對我們造成負面影響。
我們可能無法識別並完成符合我們標準之不動產收購，這可能阻礙我們之成長。
我們在收購實體不動產方面面臨激烈競爭，這可能減少可供我們選擇之收購機會，並提高這些收購之成本。
若我們無法取得額外資金，本公司之成長能力將受到限制。
抵押貸款債務義務使我們面臨被法拍之風險，這可能導致我們在抵押貸款不動產或不動產羣組上之投資損失。
我們可能無法控制營運成本，或費用可能維持不變或增加，即使收入未增加，將導致營運結果受到不利影響。
部分融資安排涉及彈性付款義務，這可能不利於我們發放現金紅利的能力。
未能有效對抗利率變動，可能不利於我們的財務狀況、營運結果、現金流及普通股每股交易價格。
我們無擔保債務的實際次級地位，可能減少用於償還無擔保債務的可支付金額。
若我們投資於房貸應收帳款，包括發放房貸，此投資將面臨多種風險，任何風險都可能降低投資價值，並導致我們遭受重大損失。
貿易政策的變化，包括課徵關稅，可能不利於我們的租戶、租賃空間的能力、開發活動及營運成本。
美國聯邦政府長時間停擺可能不利於我們部分租戶。
我們在租賃市場面臨激烈競爭，這可能降低或阻止我們物業的佔用率及租金率提高。
我們可能透過稅務延後認列交易取得不動產或不動產組合，這可能會導致股東稀釋，並限制我們出售或重新融資這些資產的能力。
Embassy Suites™，我們的特許經營商，對 Waikiki Beach Walk-Embassy Suites™ 有優先購買權，這可能會限制我們取得酒店最高價格的能力。
地震、火災、水災或其他天然災害造成的潛在損失，可能無法完全由保險賠償覆蓋。
我們可能因與氣候變遷相關的法律、法規或其他問題而受到不利影響。
氣候變遷可能直接影響我們的不動產，並可能導致額外的合規義務與成本，以及額外的稅費與費用。
paragraphs: 下列段落包含可能對我們業務與營運產生重大負面影響的最重要因素。風險因素說明了可能影響這些陳述的風險，但並非全部，尤其針對未來可能的事件。此外，我們所處的環境非常競爭且快速變動。時常會出現新的風險因素，我們無法預測所有這些風險因素，也無法評估所有這些風險因素對我們業務的影響，或任何因素，或因素組合，可能導致實際結果與任何前瞻性陳述中所包含的結果有重大差異的程度。此風險因素討論包含許多前瞻性陳述。有關依賴前瞻性陳述的警示，請參閱本報告開頭的「前瞻性陳述」部分，位於項目 1 之前。
我們的不動產組合取決於區域與地方經濟狀況，且地理上集中於加利福尼亞州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、德克薩斯州與夏威夷州，這可能使我們比擁有更地理多樣化組合的情況下更容易受到這些市場不利發展的影響。

我們的不動產位於加利福尼亞州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、德克薩斯州與夏威夷州，且我們的不動產幾乎全部集中於加利福尼亞州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州與夏威夷州，這使我們面臨較高的經濟風險，如果我們擁有更地理多樣化的組合，風險將較低。因此，我們特別容易受到這些市場的經濟或其他條件不利影響（例如經濟放緩或衰退、企業裁員或縮編、產業放緩、地方或全球旅遊產業的變化、企業遷移、房地產及其他稅收增加，以及符合政府規範或增加規範的成本），以及這些市場發生的自然災害（例如地震、野火、熱帶氣旋、颶風、龍捲風及其他事件）的影響。如果這些市場經濟出現衰退，我們的營運與營收及可用於分配的現金，包括可用於支付分紅給美國資產信託股份有限公司股東或美國資產信託有限責任公司單位持有人的現金，可能受到重大不利影響。我們無法保證這些市場會成長，或這些市場的房地產基礎設施對辦公室、零售、混合用途或多戶住宅不動產的所有者與經營者而言是有利的。如果這些市場中興建了競爭性不動產，我們的營運也可能受到影響。此外，我們核心市場中的次市場可能依賴於極少數產業。另外，加利福尼亞州被認為是較容易發生法律訴訟、高度管制且稅收較高的州，所有這些因素都可能降低加利福尼亞州辦公室、零售、混合用途或多戶住宅空間的需求。任何加利福尼亞州、華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、德克薩斯州或夏威夷州的經濟或房地產不利發展，或因規範環境、商業氣候或能源或財政問題導致辦公室、零售、多戶住宅或混合用途空間需求減少，都可能對我們的財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、我們履行債務償還義務的能力，以及我們支付分紅給美國資產信託股份有限公司股東或美國資產信託有限責任公司單位持有人的能力產生不利影響。

2025 年，我們約 52% 的淨營業收入來自辦公室不動產。在家工作、彈性工作時段、開放式辦公空間、視訊會議及電話會議已成為常見做法，特別是因應疫情的影響。這些做法可能使企業減少對辦公室空間的需求。同時，一些企業也逐漸傾向使用共享辦公空間與共創辦公空間。這些做法持續的趨勢，可能在長遠時間內削弱辦公室空間的總體需求，進而對使用率、租金率與不動產價值產生向下壓力，這可能對我們的財務狀況、營運結果與現金流產生不利影響。

2026 年 2 月 6 日，我們的總負債（不含發行費用）約為 1.70 十億美元，其中一部分包含非追索權除外擔保與環境賠償，由我們與我們的營運合夥企業提供，我們可能因未來的收購與開發活動而產生大量額外負債。2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們也有一項第三修正與重述的信貸協議，信貸額度為 5 億美元，包含 4 億美元的循環信貸線與 1 億美元的無擔保貸款（貸款 A）。償還貸款的本金與利息可能使我們缺乏足夠的現金資源來營運不動產或支付目前預期或必要的分紅，以維持我們的 REIT 資格。我們的負債水平與債務協議對我們的限制可能產生重大不利後果，包括以下項目：
• 我們的現金流可能不足以支付我們的本金與利息償還義務；
